## What The Business Is

Lam Research is a Fremont, California–based semiconductor capital equipment company that supplies wafer-fabrication equipment and services used to make advanced chips; the company says nearly every advanced chip is built with Lam technology. ([investor.lamresearch.com](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-04-22-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-March-29%2C-2026?asPDF=)) Its business is tied to wafer-fab equipment spending cycles across foundry/logic, DRAM, NAND, advanced packaging, and installed-base support.

## What It Does

Lam’s core systems revenue comes from equipment for deposition, etch, and other wafer-fabrication steps, while customer-support revenue includes service, spares, upgrades, and non-leading-edge Reliant tools. ([investor.lamresearch.com](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-04-22-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-March-29%2C-2026?asPDF=)) In the April 22, 2026 transcript excerpt, management emphasized that AI-driven device scaling is increasing etch and deposition intensity, especially in high-layer-count NAND, 1C-and-beyond DRAM, leading-edge foundry/logic, and advanced packaging. The company also highlighted its Customer Support Business Group, Dextro maintenance cobots, equipment-intelligence services, and a large installed base of more than 100,000 chambers as recurring support opportunities.

## Recent Highlights (Positive)

Lam reported a record March 2026 quarter: revenue of **$5.84 billion**, up **9% sequentially**, with non-GAAP gross margin of **49.9%**, non-GAAP operating margin of **35.0%**, and non-GAAP diluted EPS of **$1.47**. ([investor.lamresearch.com](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-04-22-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-March-29%2C-2026?asPDF=)) The quarter also showed broad support-business strength: customer support-related revenue was **$2.11 billion**, up from **$1.99 billion** in December 2025 and **$1.68 billion** a year earlier. ([investor.lamresearch.com](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-04-22-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-March-29%2C-2026?asPDF=)) Management guided the June 2026 quarter to **$6.60 billion ± $400 million** of revenue, **50.5% ± 1%** gross margin, **36.5% ± 1%** operating margin, and **$1.65 ± $0.15** EPS, indicating expected sequential acceleration. ([investor.lamresearch.com](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-04-22-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-March-29%2C-2026?asPDF=)) The transcript also raised the company’s 2026 wafer-fab-equipment view to about **$140 billion** with “bias to the upside,” cited NAND conversion spending being pulled forward, record DRAM revenue, foundry/logic etch wins, and advanced-packaging revenue expected to grow more than 50% in calendar 2026. Lam also declared a **$0.26** quarterly dividend payable **July 8, 2026** to holders of record on **June 17, 2026**. ([prnewswire.com](https://www.prnewswire.com/news-releases/lam-research-corporation-declares-quarterly-dividend-302779518.html?utm_source=openai))

## Recent Highlights (Negative)

China remains a major exposure: Lam’s March 2026 quarter revenue mix was **34% China**, and the transcript excerpt says management expected China revenue to decline in the June quarter. ([investor.lamresearch.com](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-04-22-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-March-29%2C-2026?asPDF=)) The company’s own cautionary language flags that trade regulations, export controls, tariffs, trade disputes, geopolitical tensions, supply-chain cost increases, and manufacturing-capacity constraints could inhibit sales or pressure profitability. ([investor.lamresearch.com](https://investor.lamresearch.com/2026-04-22-Lam-Research-Corporation-Reports-Financial-Results-for-the-Quarter-Ended-March-29%2C-2026?asPDF=)) Policy risk also stayed active in the last 90 days: reporting on April 17, 2026 said U.S. lawmakers narrowed proposed MATCH Act restrictions affecting chipmaking tools, including cryogenic etch equipment, but noted China-related export-control limits already constrain access to such tools.
